<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Current state: White F at [11, 20], Green F at [29, 41]
# Need to move white F to overlap green F
# White F center is roughly at row 18, col 24 (based on boundary [[11, 20], [11, 28], [25, 28], [25, 20]])
# Green F center is roughly at row 39, col 45 (based on boundary [[29, 41], [29, 49], [49, 49], [49, 41]])

# Each move is 3 rows/cols
# To go from row ~18 to row ~39: need 7 DOWN (21 rows)
# To go from col ~24 to col ~45: need 7 RIGHT (21 cols)

# But let me be more precise. White F boundary is [[11, 20], [11, 28], [25, 28], [25, 20]]
# So white F spans rows 11-25, cols 20-28
# Green F spans rows 29-49, cols 41-49

# To overlap, white F top-left [11, 20] needs to move to [29, 41]
# That's 18 rows down (6 DOWN moves) and 21 cols right (7 RIGHT moves)

# Let me try: 6 DOWN, 7 RIGHT, then SPACE
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
w_node = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'W' and n['pixels'] > 10][0]
n_node = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'N' and n['pixels'] > 10][0]
print(f"White F: {w_node['boundary']}")
print(f"Green F: {n_node['boundary']}")

# Move white F to overlap green F
actions = ['DOWN'] * 6 + ['RIGHT'] * 7 + ['SPACE']
print(f"Executing: {actions}")
result = action(actions)
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
print("\nAfter moves:")
for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] != 'S':
        print(f"  {n['color']} id={n['id']}: pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary'][:4]}")
print(f"level_completed={result.get('level_completed')}, done={result.get('done')}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
